description: Top management demonstrates leadership and commitment to the AI management system, including setting an AI policy.
Roles, responsibilities, and authorities relevant to the AI management system are assigned and communicated.
A process exists to assess risks and opportunities specific to AI systems, including impacts on individuals and groups.
AI system impact assessments are performed considering potential consequences for individuals, groups, and society.
Resources needed for the AI management system, including competent personnel and infrastructure, are identified and provided.
Personnel are competent and aware of the AI policy, their contribution, and implications of non-conformity.
Operational planning and control exist for AI system development, deployment, and decommissioning across the lifecycle.
Processes govern the quality, provenance, and suitability of data used to develop and operate AI systems.
Risks arising from third-party and supplier relationships involved in AI systems are identified and managed.
The performance and effectiveness of the AI management system are monitored, measured, analysed, and evaluated.
Internal audits are conducted at planned intervals to assess conformance of the AI management system.
Top management reviews the AI management system at planned intervals to ensure continuing suitability and effectiveness.
Nonconformities are addressed and opportunities for continual improvement of the AI management system are pursued.
